messages:
Zoe Park: Hey team  onboarding question. I'm indexing a corpus and want to run an embeddings batch: ~120k short docs over ~2 hours. Should I use a sandbox key or request a hosted burst? Worried about per-minute embedding quotas and token limits per request.
Leah Morgan: Welcome Zoe! Sandbox usually has tight embeddings quotas and different model variants. For a run that size we recommend a hosted ephemeral window or chunking into many smaller jobs. What model + concurrency are you planning?
Zoe Park: Plan is redwood-embed-large, batches of ~200 items, concurrency ~4 from a single GH runner, ~8k requests/hour. Prefer deterministic run w/o 429s.
Carlos Rivera: Ops can provision a temporary hosted quota for batch indexing. File an OPS ticket with start/end, total items, batch size, concurrency, model and estimated embedding units. For high-volume we also advise using our shared CI NAT to simplify whitelisting.
Zoe Park: Is there a quick CLI to check if my key is sandbox vs hosted and current quota?
Leah Morgan: Yep:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me | jq '.key_type, .quota'
```
That returns "hosted" or "sandbox" plus quota buckets. Console -> Usage -> API Keys also shows per-key embedding units and remaining.
Zoe Park: Any recommended batch size? Docs say up to 1024 items per request but memory might be an issue.
Carlos Rivera: 200-500 is a pragmatic sweet spot. 200 keeps memory sane and allows you to parallelize. Note we meter embedding units = tokens * items, so include estimated units in the ticket (helps ops & billing).
ops-bot: File OPS ticket at ops-team@redwood.ai with details. Include billing owner for costs >$100.
Billing Bot: Heads up  embeddings at this scale can burn onboarding credits quickly. Please include manager approval if unsure.
Zoe Park: Filing OPS-5102: "Embeddings bulk run 120k items, 2026-03-27 06:00-08:00 UTC, model redwood-embed-large, batch 200, concurrency 4, est units 7.2M". CC Carlos.
Carlos Rivera: Got it. A couple of testing tips: to emulate hitting per-key limits in CI use header `X-Test-Force-429: after=50` or our quota emulator header `X-Emulate-Quota: units=5000` which returns 429 once the emulated units are consumed. Don't use the emulator for perf numbers.
Zoe Park: Great. How should I monitor progress and alerts during the run?
Leah Morgan: Console -> Usage -> Embeddings shows per-key unit consumption near real-time. You can also poll `/v1/usage/key`. For long jobs set an alert in Console -> Alerts: e.g., 429 rate > 3% over 5m or units consumed > X.
Zoe Park: OPS-5102 marked pending billing approval. Thanks all, will wait for the hosted window and whitelist instructions.
Carlos Rivera: We'll approve once billing confirms. We'll also suggest throttles if needed and can provide two ephemeral keys if you want to rotate mid-run.
Zoe Park: Perfect, thanks everyone!
